condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Verapamil, the closest structural analog with the same dimethoxyphenyl tertiary-amine motif, has measured absolute oral F values of 22–52% in cirrhosis patients, all at or above the 20% threshold.
Valbenazine, which shares a dimethoxy-substituted fused bicyclic core and a basic amine, has an absolute oral bioavailability of approximately 49% in humans.

L5 gut-wall/intestinal records show verapamil is a high-permeability compound with essentially complete intestinal absorption in human intestinal perfusion and high Caco-2 Papp, with P-gp efflux playing only a minor role due to high passive permeability.
The only sub-20% F records (alfentanil 1%, rat sulpiride 15%) come from structurally dissimilar or species-limited contexts and do not outweigh the human analog evidence.

Verapamil's low oral bioavailability is attributed mainly to extensive first-pass metabolism rather than gut-wall efflux, but its measured F values remain ≥20%, so this does not provide affirmative sub-20% evidence for the query.

evidence_gaps: No direct experimental oral bioavailability measurement exists for the query molecule itself.
No matched IV comparator or absolute F study is available for the query.
First-pass metabolism and lactam stability of the query are unknown.
No formulation, dose, or fed/fasted data are available for the query.
Transfer relies on structural analogy to verapamil and valbenazine; the query's rigid lactam/carbocycle may alter absorption or metabolism.
No human intestinal perfusion or Caco-2 permeability data exist for the query itself.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high (F ≥ 20%) because the most transferable human contexts (verapamil, valbenazine) show absolute F values of approximately 22–52%, L4/L5 records confirm verapamil-like high intestinal permeability and essentially complete absorption with minor efflux limitation, and no affirmative sub-20% evidence applies to the query; confidence remains moderate because no direct F measurement exists for the query.
